# Blender handoff

What the Blender side builds, what it receives, and what it must hand back. Conventions are in [CONVENTIONS.md](CONVENTIONS.md): metres, Z-up, right-handed, poses 4x4 camera-to-world.

## Inputs (generated by the Python side; ask Laiba for the files or pull via DVC)
- `data/processed/bim/elements.npz`: for each element `<guid>__v` (N x 3 vertices, metres, world coords) and `<guid>__f` (M x 3 triangle indices).
- `data/processed/bim/elements.json`: guid, ifc_class, name, storey, elevation_m, bbox_min, bbox_max, height_m (12 elements).
- `data/synthetic/schedule_plan.csv`, `schedule_actual.csv`, `epoch_NN/gt_status.csv` (epoch days 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60).
- Assets in `data/raw/assets/` (characters, ppe_models, props, hdri). Licences in [ASSETS.md](ASSETS.md).

Blender's own Python has no IfcOpenShell. Import from the npz (numpy is bundled with Blender); do not import OBJ, because of its axis options. Vertices go straight through, no rotation.

## Scripts to write (in `scripts/blender/`)
1. **`inspect_assets.py`** - for each asset print size in metres, polycount, rig and animations. Fix scale and units here. Open question: does the construction-worker GLB have a skeleton, or is it a static pose? X Bot has a rig but no animation; walking clips come from Mixamo.
2. **`import_elements.py`** - one object per element, named by GlobalId. Check against the IFC visually (Bonsai is optional). Origin of each object at the base of its bounding box so scaling in Z grows it upward.
3. **`build_epoch.py <epoch>`** - from `gt_status.csv`: hide `not_started`, show `done`, and for `in_progress` scale the element along Z by `fraction` (walls and columns by height, slabs by thickness) about its base. Rendering must follow the **actual** schedule; `gt_status.csv` already encodes it.
4. **Realism** - concrete/brick textures, sun and sky from the HDRI, ground plane with dirt, props (fence, barricades, truck), slight lighting change between epochs. COLMAP fails on blank surfaces, so every element needs texture. Place a few ArUco markers at known coordinates (used for scale checking).
5. **`render_epochs.py`** - per epoch, orbit the building at 2 or 3 heights, 60-100 frames, 70-80% overlap, 1280x720, fixed seed. Time one test frame first and report the render budget (GPU machine if the laptop is too slow).

## Outputs per epoch
```
data/synthetic/epoch_NN/
  images/000001.png ...      RGB
  depth/000001.npy ...       float32 depth along the camera z axis, metres (EXR also fine)
  ids/000001.png ...         object-index mask; table object_index -> GlobalId in ids.json
  cameras.json               see below
  gt_status.csv              copied unchanged from the Python side
```
`cameras.json`:
```json
{"width": 1280, "height": 720,
 "K": [[fx,0,cx],[0,fy,cy],[0,0,1]],
 "frames": [{"id": "000001", "T_wc": [[...4x4...]]}]}
```
- `T_wc` is **camera-to-world in the OpenCV convention** (x right, y down, z forward). Blender cameras look down -Z with Y up, so flip the Y and Z axes of the camera axes.
- `fx = focal_mm * width_px / sensor_width_mm` (check the sensor fit), `cx = width/2`, `cy = height/2`.
- Same intrinsics for all frames unless stated.

## Phase 2b: safety clips (after the epoch renders work)
A separate small scene at an open slab edge. Animated characters with and without helmet/vest (attach `hard_hat` to the head bone and `hi_vis_vest` to the chest; colour variants by material). Per frame export RGB, depth, camera pose, and the **true 3D position** of each worker and each hazard zone in the BIM frame (metres), so hazard-distance error can be measured. Include near-miss clips (worker approaching the slab edge) and ground-truth PPE labels per worker.

## Performance notes
The barricade (38 MB) and the worker (30 MB) are heavy: decimate or instance them, and do not repeat full-resolution copies across the scene.

## Acceptance check
Laiba runs the Python side on one epoch: COLMAP reconstructs it, the aligned model matches `gt_status.csv`, and rendered depth agrees with COLMAP up to scale. Report anything that breaks that.
